title: Onboarding Conductor — wireframes, operator checkpoints, and error-mode runbook
summary: Working notes and wireframe concepts for the 'Onboarding Conductor' - a guided admin flow that coordinates VPC setup, region selection, network validation, and KMS/HSM key sync for Private deployments. Emphasis on operator checkpoints and explicit recovery flows for common failure modes.
body:
Context and goal:
The 'Onboarding Conductor' is intended to be a single, opinionated admin flow in the Private control plane that guides infra/ops teams through everything required to bring a Private deployment online: choose region, validate quotas, set up VPC peering or transit, configure route tables/firewall rules, and import/register KMS keys or HSM credentials. The goal is to dramatically reduce the 'unknown unknowns' operators hit during first-time setup and to provide deterministic recovery steps when external systems fail (cloud quotas, key import, HSM provisioning).

High-level flow (wireframe panels):
1) Intro / Preflight
   - Short checklist: account owner, subscription/tenant ID, desired region, expected RPS, compliance tier.
   - Quick link to a generated runbook PDF for the customer's security team.
   - CTA: Start conductor / Save and continue later.

2) Region & capacity checker
   - UI shows chosen region(s) with inline latency/throughput guidance (estimated TTFB for x GPUs).
   - Inline check: account quotas API call (async). If quota low -> show exact quota delta and one-click open support case pre-filled.

3) Network topology selector
   - Two-mode toggle: Peering vs. Customer gateway (transit).
   - Wireframe: visual canvas with minimal nodes: Customer VPC(s), Redwood Private VPC, optional Edge Router.
   - Auto-populate recommended route table/fwt rules with copy/paste ready terraform/snippets.

4) Network validation (operator checkpoint)
   - Run validation: checks for route overlap, overlapping CIDRs, missing IGW/NAT rules, required ports (gRPC/443).
   - Failure states: show specific actionable remediation and a recommended command/snippet.
   - If validation fails, put conductor into 'paused' state and offer: Retry validation / Mark manual-complete & continue / Open troubleshooting session (screen share link template).

5) Key material import and HSM provisioning
   - Option A: Bring-your-own KMS key (import) -> step-by-step: export public key, sign CSR, provide key alias, confirm key policies.
   - Option B: Redwood-managed HSM integration (customer gives admin endpoint + cert) -> handshake flow + attestation check.
   - UX: progress spinner with detailed logs, and a delayed validation poll (up to 10 minutes).

6) Finalize and bootstrap
   - Confirm region, network, key assignment.
   - Bootstrap job runs (provision compute, model bundles, routing).
   - Post-bootstrap checklist: smoke test, token rotation, access audit.

Operator checkpoints and error-mode designs:
- 'Paused' conductor: when an external dependency errors (quota, key import, HSM attestation), the UI explicitly enters a paused state. This prevents partial bootstrap and leaves the operator with three clear choices: retry, manual-ack (operator certifies they've fixed it), or abort & rollback.
- Persistent logs: each conductor execution attaches structured logs to the deployment record (timestamped steps + raw cloud API responses). These logs are exportable and writable to S3 for support tickets.
- Time-to-retry/backoff policy: default 1m, 3m, 10m, then operator override. Allow immediate manual retry from the UI.
- Graceful fallback for KMS failures: if customer key import fails, console proposes two fallback modes: temporary Redwood-managed key (with explicit consent and audit trail) or offline manual key sync mode (operator uploads wrapped key via secure channel). Both paths must surface risk statements and required compliance checks.

Wireframe interactions and microcopy notes:
- Use problem-focused microcopy at failure points (what happened, why, next step). Avoid generic 'failed' messages.
- When opening support case, pre-fill templates with conductor step logs, region, and job id. Offer 'include stacktrace' toggle.
- Show progress by step name (not percent) e.g., 'Validating routes', 'Attaching key', 'Bootstrapping runtime'.

Backlog grooming (tickets + rough sizing) - prioritized:
- ONB-101 (3) - Region quota check: call provider quotas API + expose exact shortfall and one-click support link. Acceptance: shows precise quota delta and prefilled support form.
- ONB-112 (5) - Network validation engine: implement route/CIDR overlap and required port check rules + UI pause state. Acceptance: fail pause path visible and retry works.
- ONB-126 (5) - Key import orchestration: implement import workflow for AWS KMS and raw PEM uploads + retry policy. Acceptance: key import can be retried without full bootstrap restart.
- ONB-137 (3) - HSM attestation probe: run attestation handshake and surfacing of exact failure codes. Acceptance: clear error codes and remediation links.
- ONB-145 (2) - Runbook PDF generator: assemble customer runbook at start and end. Acceptance: downloadable PDF contains network and key config snippets.
- ONB-152 (5) - Paused conductor UX: pause modal, manual-ack, export logs to S3. Acceptance: pause/resume flows tested with simulated failures.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- Should we allow partial bootstraps when network validation fails if operator checks 'I understand risk'? (Security says no for most enterprise customers).
- For KMS fallback to Redwood-managed key, what legal/contract text is required? Need legal review.
- HSM integrations: do we support HSM provisioning as a managed service in-region or only customer-provided HSM endpoints? (Ops prefers customer-provided for compliance).

Notes to devs:
- Keep wireframes modular: each step is an independent microflow that can be retried without restarting prior steps. That reduces blast radius for retries.
- Design API contract: conductor should return a job id and step ids so UI can poll step-level status and logs.
- Logging: include cloud provider request ids in logs for support correlation.

Next immediate actions (this doc):
- Sync with legal (Lina) for fallback key consent text (deadline 2025-11-14).
- Product/design: quick usability test of the pause/resume modal with two operators (Marco to schedule).
- Engineering: spike ONB-112 network validator and bring back API schema for step-level polling within one sprint.

Appendix: quick sketch notes
- Small left rail with steps; main canvas shows wireframe for that step; right rail shows live validation/logs and 'support' quick actions.
- Colour: red states only for blocking failures. Yellow for warnings that allow continue-with-warning.
- Keyboard-first: allow operators to copy CLI snippets quickly and accept paste-confirmations for manual fixes.

End of notes.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end onboarding can be completed by an operator following the guided conductor without needing to open console logs
When an external dependency fails the conductor enters a paused state and provides three clear, testable recovery options
Key import/HSM handshake can be retried from the UI without restarting prior validated steps
Exported runbook PDF contains the same network/key configuration used by the conductor
